summary:
Migrated backend runtime context (correlation, request/security, database QueryRunner tracking) from three independent hand-written AsyncLocalStorage instances to one shared nestjs-cls@6.2.1 infrastructure encapsulated behind a new libs/platform/context library. Public API of CorrelationContext, RequestContext and TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext/TypeOrmUnitOfWork is preserved. Each app composition root (api/worker/cli/scheduler/realtime) configures the CLS root exactly once via RuntimeContextModule.forRoot(); apps/api and apps/realtime auto-mount the HTTP CLS initializer; apps/worker opens one independent root per BullMQ job; apps/cli/apps/scheduler open roots on demand via RequestContext#runAsSystem(). A new dependency-cruiser rule enforces that libs/platform/context never depends on security/observability/database/typeorm. RuntimeContextSeed's ownership-claiming validator is a closed-world preflight: only a fully value-graph-walked plain object/array or a genuinely plain, undecorated Date may ever be seeded, with no caller-declared "trust me, this is atomic" escape hatch (removed at attempt 27 -- fix-request review cycle 15 finding #1), so no value graph the public seed API accepts can expose shared mutable state across two roots. Every changed characterization-sensitive implementation has a recorded legacy-baseline test run against the frozen origin/master@c8ca980 source (evidence/characterization-baseline.md, [characterization-baseline: v9]).

Current validated state: lint, typecheck, [unit-tests: 69 suites / 448 tests], all 5 application builds, test:architecture (474 modules / 1794 deps / 0 violations), migration:run + db:seed, [e2e-tests: 20 suites / 146 tests], and the legacy characterization harness ([characterization-tests: 5 suites / 30 tests]) all pass fresh against a rebuilt throwaway real Postgres/Redis/MinIO stack. libs/platform/context/test/runtime-context.service.spec.ts has [context-spec-cases: 59] cases. Full per-review-cycle implementation history is in decisions[] below and handoff_status.review_state; this summary intentionally states each fact once, tagged `[name: value]`, rather than accumulating superseded numbers -- ai/skills/review-vertical-slice-completeness/scripts/check_evidence_freshness.py deterministically rejects any future attempt that lets a tagged fact drift out of sync with itself or with the artifact it describes.

decisions.decision: libs/platform/context exposes a generic typed-namespace facade (RuntimeContextService for DI, RuntimeContextAccessor as its static/non-DI mirror) instead of any domain-aware store type.
decisions.reason: Task requires the library to own no CorrelationStore/RequestContextStore/QueryRunner type. Each owning module (observability/security/database) supplies its own namespace key string ('correlation'/'request'/'database') and casts with its own type parameter at the call site, keeping type safety at the facade boundary without a reverse or circular dependency.

decisions.decision: RuntimeContextService.runNested() always opens a genuinely new AsyncLocalStorage frame (nestjs-cls ClsService#run with an explicit ifNested policy — never the implicit default) rather than mutating the active store in place; RuntimeContextService.runRoot() always opens a brand-new context via ClsService#runWith regardless of ambient state.
decisions.reason: This is what makes 'scoped override never mutates a parent-owned object' and 'a job/command root never inherits an ambient context' true by construction rather than by convention. Verified directly in libs/platform/context/test/runtime-context.service.spec.ts (11 cases: inherit/override/reuse policies, sibling preservation, parent restore on success and on throw, concurrent isolation).

decisions.decision: CorrelationContext and RequestContext each got a new seedActiveRoot()/RequestContext#seedActiveRoot() method, used only by CorrelationMiddleware/RequestContextMiddleware, distinct from the existing run()/RequestContext#run() nested-override facade.
decisions.reason: The task explicitly forbids HTTP middleware from calling the generic run() facade to create a second root/nested frame for the request ('Middleware không gọi facade run() để tạo root mới'), while the same run() facade must still support true nested-override-with-restore semantics for its other callers. seedActiveRoot() writes directly into the already-active root when one exists (no new frame — matches the existing 'root enrichment mutates the current object' pattern JwtAuthGuard already relies on) and only falls back to opening a root itself when none is active yet (preserves the original correlation-context.spec.ts / a bare 'new RequestContext()' unit-test characterization).

decisions.decision: BullMqWorkerRunner.process() now injects RuntimeContextService and calls runtimeContext.runRoot({correlation: {...}}, ...) directly instead of CorrelationContext.run(...).
decisions.reason: AC13 requires each job's root to be guaranteed independent of any ambient context — runRoot() is unconditional (ClsService#runWith), whereas CorrelationContext.run()'s nested-with-fallback semantics would only coincidentally behave the same way if nothing happened to be ambient when BullMQ invoked the processor. Regression-tested for both 'never inherits an ambient HTTP-producer-shaped context' and 'two concurrent jobs never observe each other' in libs/platform/queue/test/bullmq.worker.correlation.spec.ts.

decisions.decision: Each app.module.ts imports RuntimeContextModule.forRoot() as the first entry in its `imports` array, before ObservabilityModule/SecurityModule; apps/api and apps/realtime additionally pass { mountHttpMiddleware: true }.
decisions.reason: Nest applies module-registered middleware in the order their configure() hooks run, which this codebase already relied on before this migration (see the pre-existing comment in security.module.ts about ObservabilityModule needing to precede SecurityModule for CorrelationMiddleware to run before RequestContextMiddleware). Rather than trust that assumption for the new CLS initializer without proof, it was verified empirically end-to-end (not just by reasoning) in libs/platform/security/test/http-context-lifecycle.spec.ts, which boots RuntimeContextModule + ObservabilityModule + SecurityModule in the exact apps/api import order and asserts, via supertest against a live in-memory Nest app, that RuntimeContextAccessor.isActive() is already true and correlation/request are already seeded by the time the controller runs, headers echo unchanged, and two concurrent requests never observe each other. All three assertions passed on the first run, confirming automatic mount is sufficient here and manual bootstrap mounting is not required.

decisions.decision: Namespace access on RuntimeContextService/RuntimeContextAccessor now takes an opaque RuntimeContextKey<T> token (created once via createRuntimeContextKey<T>(namespace) by the owning module) instead of a bare namespace string; runRoot() takes a RuntimeContextSeed builder (.set(key, value)) instead of an untyped Record<string, unknown>.
decisions.reason: fix-request-review-001 finding #1: the prior string-keyed getNamespace<T>(namespace)/setNamespace<T>(namespace, value) let a caller independently choose any T at each call site (e.g. getNamespace<RequestContextStore>('database') would have compiled), so type safety was not actually enforced at the platform facade boundary despite each namespace being domain-owned. RuntimeContextKey<T> carries T only as a compile-time phantom field (never assigned/read at runtime, so platform/context still never imports CorrelationStore/RequestContextStore/QueryRunner) — TypeScript then rejects passing a value or a get/setNamespace call that does not match the exact T the key was declared with. Compile-time proof added in libs/platform/context/test/runtime-context.service.spec.ts (`@ts-expect-error` cases: a RequestLikeStore value rejected for a correlation-typed key, a string value rejected for a request-typed key, and one key's type rejected at another key's call site) plus a positive case proving getNamespace<T>() infers exactly T, not unknown/any. Each owning module (observability/security/database) declares its own key next to its store type; CORRELATION_CONTEXT_KEY is exported from observability (public API) so BullMqWorkerRunner — which already depends on @memories/platform/observability for MetricsRegistry — can seed the correlation slice of a job's brand-new root through the same typed key instead of an untyped string; REQUEST_CONTEXT_KEY/DATABASE_CONTEXT_KEY stay module-private since no other platform library needs to seed those namespaces directly.

decisions.decision: Attempt 16: RequestContext.run() and CorrelationContext.run() now check RuntimeContextAccessor.isActive() BEFORE opening the nested CLS frame, and bind the namespace to an isolated clone of the caller-supplied store (built by the new cloneRequestContextStore() helper for RequestContextStore — new top-level object plus new roles/permissions array instances; an inline { ...store } spread for the flat CorrelationStore) whenever that check found a parent already active. When no parent is active (the temporary-root fallback path), the original reference is still bound directly and uncloned, so the pre-existing `expect(requestContext.get()).toBe(store)` top-level (non-nested) characterization test continues to pass unchanged.
decisions.reason: fix-request-review-004 finding #1 (major, AC9/AC10): both facades previously bound the exact object reference passed to run() into the nested frame's namespace slot. Nesting run() with the parent's own currently-active store back in as the argument (`run(this.get()!, ...)`), or with a shallow copy that still shared the parent's roles/permissions array identity, meant mutations made inside the nested callback were visible on the parent's object once the nested call returned — on both the success and throw paths, since the mutation happened via the shared reference itself, not via the CLS restore mechanism (which correctly restores which *object* is active per frame, but was never told to protect the *contents* of an object handed to it directly). Cloning only conditionally (parent-active) rather than unconditionally preserves the existing reference-identity characterization test for the non-nested/no-active-parent path while closing the leak for every nested case, matching the fix-request's suggested approach exactly. 5 new tests added (3 in request-context.spec.ts covering same-reference-across-nested-run on success and throw plus a shallow-copy-aliased-roles/permissions case; 2 in correlation-context.spec.ts covering same-reference-across-nested-run on success and throw) — all pass, and the full existing 30-case (25 pre-existing + 5 new) request-context.spec.ts/correlation-context.spec.ts suite remains green. Also fixed the accompanying AC21 doc-consistency gap in ai/domains/request-context/overview.md (outside the backend worktree, not part of evidence/provenance's hashed inputs), whose terminology table previously implied worker/scheduler jobs receive SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID the same way CLI does — corrected to match the accurate per-transport semantics already documented in request-context.ts's code comments since attempt 7.

decisions.decision: Attempt 17: RuntimeContextService.runRoot() now binds `{ ...rawSeedRecord(seed) }` (a fresh top-level object snapshotting the seed's accumulated values at the exact moment runRoot is called) to `ClsService#runWith`, instead of passing `rawSeedRecord(seed)` — the seed's own persistent WeakMap-backed record — directly.
decisions.reason: fix-request-review-005 finding #1 (major, AC1/AC7/AC14/AC19): a RuntimeContextSeed's raw record is a single persistent object living in the module-private `seedRecords` WeakMap (one object per seed instance, mutated in place by every `.set()` call). Passing that same object reference straight into `runWith` meant a root's CLS store WAS that persistent object, not a copy of it — so calling `.set()` on the seed again after an earlier `runRoot(seed, ...)` had already started (including concurrently, before the first callback resolves) mutated the already-active root's live store out from under it, and reusing the same seed instance for a second `runRoot` call bound the identical object as the second root's store too, aliasing both roots to one another. The reproduction in the fix-request (two concurrent runRoot calls sharing one seed, set to 'A' then 'B') demonstrated the first execution observing the second's write. Snapshotting at call time closes this for the top-level record unconditionally — every runRoot call gets an object nothing else can reach — while remaining backward compatible with every existing legitimate seed usage (each of which already constructs a fresh `new RuntimeContextSeed()` per call and passes it exactly once). Only the individual namespace *values* inside the record are still carried by reference (unchanged from before — same as any other object argument), which is outside this finding's reproduction and consistent with how CorrelationContext/RequestContext already handle their own separate mutable-reference-isolation concern (attempt 16) at their own layer. 2 new tests added to runtime-context.service.spec.ts: a concurrent-reuse case reproducing the exact review scenario (asserts A,A/B,B, not the previously-possible A,B/B,B) and a sequential-reuse case proving a completed root's in-callback `setNamespace` mutation cannot alter a later root opened from the same reused seed.

decisions.decision: Attempt 18: `RuntimeContextSeed` is now single-use. `runRoot()` consumes a seed's record via the new `consumeSeedRecord(seed)` friend accessor — which marks the seed permanently consumed and returns its record directly (no copy needed, since consumption guarantees exclusive access) — synchronously, before its `callback` ever runs; both a later `runRoot(seed, ...)` and a later `seed.set(...)` against the same instance throw `RuntimeContextSeed already consumed by runRoot()`. `rawSeedRecord()` and its top-level-spread call site in `runRoot()` are removed entirely.
decisions.reason: fix-request-review-006 finding #1 (major, AC1/AC7/AC9/AC10/AC19): attempt 17's `{ ...rawSeedRecord(seed) }` fix only copied the seed record's top-level keys — the *value* stored under each key (e.g. the `{ requestId: 'A' }` object itself) was still the exact same object shared by every copy taken from that seed. Two roots opened from one reused seed therefore still aliased each other through that shared value object: mutating it in place from inside one root's callback (`getNamespace(key).value = 'B'`, as opposed to replacing the reference via `setNamespace`) was observable from the other root and from the seed's own future `.set()`/reads, reproduced exactly as the fix-request describes. The fix-request explicitly rules out deep-cloning every namespace value (would silently corrupt a non-cloneable domain value a namespace is allowed to carry, such as a TypeORM `QueryRunner`) and instead lists 'consume each RuntimeContextSeed exactly once with deterministic reuse rejection' as an acceptable outcome. Making the seed single-use closes the reproduction at its root: since a seed can never back more than one root's storage, there is no second root left for a shared value object to leak into, and no post-consumption `.set()` left to retroactively mutate an already-bound root. Consumption happens synchronously inside `runRoot()`'s own call (before `cls.runWith`'s callback runs, even if that callback is later awaited), so a second `runRoot(seed, ...)` call issued immediately afterward is rejected deterministically — it can never race the first callback for access to a shared value, which is exactly the ordering guarantee the fix-request's 'Done when' criterion asks for. Every production call site (RequestContext#seedActiveRoot, CorrelationContext#run's temporary-root fallback, BullMqWorkerRunner#process) already constructs `new RuntimeContextSeed().set(...)` fresh inline per `runRoot()` call — grep-verified — so this tightening changes no real caller's behavior; only test code previously exercised (and now tests the rejection of) reuse. 3 tests replace the old 'seed reuse (review #5)' describe block in runtime-context.service.spec.ts: concurrent-reuse rejection (proves the second `runRoot()` throws synchronously before the first root's pending callback resolves, and that an in-place mutation made after consumption cannot reach a second root because none is ever opened), sequential-reuse rejection (a seed stays consumed even after its one root has already completed), and a retained fresh-seed-per-call isolation case (unaffected — proves normal concurrent usage, each with its own seed, is unchanged).

decisions.decision: Attempt 18: `cloneRequestContextStore()` (libs/platform/security/src/request-context.ts) now also reconstructs `requestedAt` as `new Date(store.requestedAt.getTime())`, alongside its existing `roles`/`permissions` array clones.
decisions.reason: fix-request-review-006 finding #2 (major, AC9/AC10): the clone helper introduced in attempt 16 (fix-request-review-004) copied the top-level object and the two mutable arrays but left `requestedAt` pointing at the parent's own `Date` instance — `Date` methods like `setUTCFullYear` mutate in place, so a nested `RequestContext.run()` override that touched `requestedAt` (directly, or via a shallow copy whose `requestedAt` still aliased the parent's) still changed the parent's own store, reproduced exactly as the fix-request describes (nesting `run(get()!, ...)` then `requestedAt.setUTCFullYear(2030)` changed the parent from 2026 to 2030). Reconstructing a new `Date` from the same timestamp gives the clone an independent, mutation-safe instance while preserving the exact moment in time. Every mutable member of `RequestContextStore` (`roles`, `permissions`, `requestedAt`) now has an explicit, owner-specific isolation strategy in this one helper; every other field is a primitive or `null`, already safe under the top-level `{ ...store }` spread. 3 new tests added to request-context.spec.ts's mutable-reference-isolation suite, mirroring the existing roles/permissions same-reference and shallow-copy cases: same-reference nested run() mutating `requestedAt` on success, on throw, and a shallow-copy-aliased-`requestedAt` case.

decisions.decision: Attempt 25: claimValueOwnership() (libs/platform/context/src/runtime-context.types.ts) now recursively walks the complete reachable value graph of a value passed to RuntimeContextSeed.set() — via a new isTraversableContainer() boundary that only recurses into plain objects/arrays, with a cycle-safe `seen` set guarding self-referential graphs within one call — claiming every reachable node, instead of only the top-level reference.
decisions.reason: fix-request-review-013 finding #1 (major, AC1/AC7/AC9/AC10/AC19): review #10's fix made ownership claims permanent across seeds, but only for the exact value passed to .set() itself — two distinct, individually never-reused top-level wrapper objects that both merely CONTAINED the same nested mutable object/array/Date still passed that check, while the two roots they opened still shared the nested reference and could observe each other's mutation through it. The reviewer's reproduction (`{nested: shared}` seeded into two different seeds via two different wrapper objects) confirmed exactly this: {seenA:['A','B'],seenB:['A','B'],shared:{value:'B'}} instead of isolated A/A and B/B. Deep-cloning every reachable value was rejected as a fix strategy from review #6 onward (would silently corrupt non-cloneable domain values a namespace is allowed to carry, e.g. a TypeORM QueryRunner) — the fix-request's suggested approach explicitly asked for an ownership boundary covering the complete mutable value graph 'without blindly cloning non-cloneable infrastructure objects' and to 'explicitly define supported atomic/non-cloneable values'. isTraversableContainer() is exactly that boundary: only object-literal-shaped objects (Object.prototype or null prototype) and arrays are walked into; any other reference type (Date, QueryRunner, Map, any class instance, a function) is claimed as a single atomic leaf and never traversed, so this library never has to understand or touch an infrastructure object's internals. 7 new regression tests added to runtime-context.service.spec.ts's new 'cross-seed nested value graph ownership' describe block: shared nested object (concurrent reproduction matching the reviewer's exact scenario, plus sequential), shared nested array, shared nested Date, a production-shaped RequestContextStore-like case with two independent stores sharing the same `roles` array (the exact real-world shape this finding's 'Tests to add/change' asked for), an atomic non-cloneable instance (a self-referential QueryRunner-shaped class) proven claimed-as-a-reference-but-never-walked-into-or-corrupted, and a self-referential plain-object graph proven not to infinite-loop. Every production call site (RequestContext#seedActiveRoot, CorrelationContext#run's temporary-root fallback, BullMqWorkerRunner#process) already constructs an entirely fresh value graph inline per runRoot() call — grep-verified — so this tightening changes no real caller's behavior.
